title: Planning with HTN and Evolutionary Search

questions.question: What does an HTN add over a free-form LLM plan?
options: Shorter prompts, since the planner skips few-shot worked examples
Provable correctness when operator preconditions and effects are enforced
Better embeddings for retrieving semantically similar past plans
Cheaper inference because the plan skips redundant LLM calls at every step
questions.explanation: HTN's symbolic operators with preconditions and effects guarantee soundness by construction.

questions.question: Which problem class is AlphaEvolve built for?
options: Multi-turn chat memory management across very long conversations
Vector search ranking over dense semantic embedding spaces
Optimizations with a machine-checkable, deterministic fitness function
Free-form prose generation tasks with no objective scoring function at all
questions.explanation: Evolutionary search needs a deterministic evaluator; AlphaEvolve targets domains where one exists.

questions.question: How does ChatHTN preserve plan soundness while using an LLM?
options: It fine-tunes the LLM directly on recorded HTN planning traces until its suggestions become reliable
It uses a vector database to retrieve the closest previously-validated plan and reuses it verbatim
It does not guarantee soundness at all; ChatHTN treats plan correctness as a best-effort heuristic to be refined through repeated user feedback
LLM suggestions only enter as candidate decompositions, validated against the operator schema; the symbolic layer owns correctness
questions.explanation: The LLM expands the method library but cannot bypass operator preconditions and effects.

questions.question: Which AlphaEvolve result does the lesson cite?
options: First improvement over Strassen for 4x4 complex matrix multiplication in 56 years
A 10x inference speedup on Gemini achieved purely through evolutionary prompt search
Beating GPT-4's score on the HumanEval code-generation benchmark
The first widely accepted computer-verified proof that P equals NP
questions.explanation: AlphaEvolve found 48 scalar multiplications for 4x4 complex matmul, the first improvement on Strassen in 56 years.

questions.question: Which element of an HTN is a primitive directly-executable action with preconditions and effects?
options: A task — compound (to be decomposed) or primitive
An operator — a primitive action with preconditions and effects
A state — a set of facts describing the world at a point in planning
A method — one of several ways to decompose a compound task into subtasks
questions.explanation: Operators are the primitives; methods decompose compound tasks; state is a set of facts.

questions.question: What is the lesson's warning about AlphaEvolve without a real evaluator?
options: Running AlphaEvolve without a machine-checkable evaluator violates the Apache 2.0 license terms
Without a dedicated evaluator, AlphaEvolve cannot execute candidate mutations on GPU hardware
Asking an LLM whether the code is better is not a fitness function; the evaluator must be deterministic and fast
AlphaEvolve without a real evaluator simply runs somewhat slower than with one, but the search still converges to a correct answer eventually
questions.explanation: Without a deterministic evaluator the search has no signal to converge on.
